title: Invariants of a transported injective resolution compute homogeneous continuous cohomology
statement:
Let $G$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group in universe $u$.
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and let
$E:\mathcal A\simeq\operatorname{DiscreteRep}_{\mathbf Z}(G)$ be an equivalence
[def-exc-discrete-modules-category], with representation universe $r=\max(u,s)$.
Let $V:\mathcal A\to\mathrm{Ab}_r$ send an object to the invariant subgroup of its
image under $E$, and send an equivariant coefficient map to its restriction on invariants.
Assume $V$ is additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Let $F\in\mathcal A$ and
$I$ be any injective resolution of $F$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions].
Let $N$ be an integer representation of $G$ on a discrete topological module in universe $r$,
and let $e:E(F)\simeq_{\mathbf Z}N$ satisfy $e(gx)=g e(x)$.
For every $q\in\mathbf N$ the underlying type of $H^q(V(I^\bullet))$ is equivalent to
$H^q_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,N)$. Here the latter is homology in topological integer modules
of the homogeneous cochain complex: degree $n$ is the $G$-invariant submodule of
$n+1$ iterated continuous-map spaces, with diagonal action
$(g f)(x)=g(f(g^{-1}x))$ and differential constant insertion minus the preceding
differential applied pointwise. No finite-ring hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Transfer open stabilizers to N through e: the stabilizer of x in N is the stabilizer of e inverse x in E(F), by equivariance and injectivity of e.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, section-continuous-group-cohomology, displayed inhomogeneous differential and final profinite comparison; parent proof steps 1-3

proof.text: Obtain the homogeneous-to-inhomogeneous term equivalences and differential formula from the coordinate lemma. Define V as forgetting a topological integer module to its underlying abelian group, and K as V applied to the homogeneous complex. Postcompose the coordinate equivalences with e inverse to obtain locally constant E(F)-valued coordinates on K. Applying e to the desired differential equation, use equivariance, preservation of addition, finite sums and integer multiples, and e composed with e inverse equals the identity.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, section-continuous-group-cohomology, displayed inhomogeneous differential and final profinite comparison; parent proof steps 1-3

proof.text: Apply the resolution-to-inhomogeneous comparison to K with those term equivalences and the proved differential equation, obtaining H^q(invariants of I) equivalent to H^q(K).

source.place: Tag 0DVG, section-continuous-group-cohomology, displayed inhomogeneous differential and final profinite comparison; parent proof steps 1-3

proof.text: The forgetful functors from topological integer modules to integer modules and then to abelian groups preserve kernels and cokernels, hence homology. Mathlib ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso for the short complex at q gives H^q(K) isomorphic to the underlying abelian group of continuousCohomology q N. Compose its underlying equivalence with the preceding one. This is the two-line categorical homology comparison, not a new unproved theorem.
